subject: anatomy
title: Stomach, spleen and coeliac trunk: key anatomy for exams

steps.tx: The **coeliac trunk** is the first anterior branch of the abdominal aorta. It arises just below the aortic hiatus, at the level of the T12 to L1 vertebral bodies, and divides into three branches: the **left gastric**, **common hepatic** and **splenic** arteries. It may also give off one or both inferior phrenic arteries.
steps.say: The coeliac trunk is the first anterior branch of the abdominal aorta. steps.tx: The **stomach bed** is formed by structures on which the posterior stomach wall rests, separated by the **lesser sac**. These include the diaphragm, left kidney, left suprarenal gland, pancreas except its tail, transverse mesocolon, splenic flexure and splenic artery. The pancreatic tail lies instead in the splenorenal ligament.

vis.caption: The stomach bed: diaphragm, left suprarenal, left kidney, pancreas, spleen, transverse mesocolon, splenic artery.

steps.tx: The **gastrosplenic ligament** joins the greater curvature to the splenic hilum and carries the short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels. It develops from the dorsal mesogastrium. The **splenorenal ligament** joins the spleen to the left kidney and carries the splenic vessels and the pancreatic tail. The spleen lies under the left diaphragm near ribs 9 to 11.

steps.tx: Stomach innervation includes the **anterior vagal trunk**, which gives the **nerve of Latarjet**, and the **posterior vagal trunk**, which gives the **nerve of Grassi** to the fundus. Vagotomy therefore affects the parasympathetic supply to the stomach. Lymph from the stomach drains to the **coeliac nodes**, and the upper left third drains via the splenic artery.

vis.caption: Anterior trunk is the left vagus; posterior trunk is the right vagus; the nerve of Grassi supplies the fundus and is cut in vagotomy.
